contexts.abstract: Teams speech experiences are converging onto a unified multilingual stack.
contexts.text: Teams speech experiences (Interpreter, Captions/Transcription) are being converged onto a unified, multilingual stack with stronger entity accuracy and reliability.

contexts.abstract: Turn‑by‑Turn Interpreter is introduced to fix SIM accuracy and flow gaps.
contexts.text: Turn‑by‑Turn (TBT) Interpreter is being introduced to solve accuracy and meeting flow gaps in interactive and structured meetings, reducing translation overlap and clarifying who is speaking.

contexts.abstract: Multilingual STT has shipped to R0/R1 with auto language detection.
contexts.text: Multilingual STT has shipped to Ring 0 and Ring 1 with a unified multi‑recognizer endpoint and automatic language detection, eliminating setup friction and enabling bilingual meetings.

contexts.abstract: Transcript Enricher is correcting high‑value meetings at scale.
contexts.text: Transcript Enricher is correcting names and domain entities in high‑value meetings at scale, with R4 rollout at 50% for EN/JP and 10% for FR/DE/PT/ES and 1.8M+ meetings weekly enhanced.

contexts.abstract: Batch S2S display models improved readability across Tier‑1 locales.
contexts.text: Batch speech‑to‑speech (S2S) display models have raised transcript readability across Tier‑1 locales without increasing cost of goods sold (CoGS).

contexts.abstract: Customers see accuracy issues on technical terms, names, and numbers.
contexts.text: Customers report accuracy issues on technical terms, names, and numbers/units, and perceive translations as too literal in simultaneous mode.
contexts.resolution_hint: Invest in entity enrichment, global/custom dictionaries, and semantic translation modes.

contexts.abstract: Latency and flow issues in SIM affect meeting experience.
contexts.text: Latency and meeting flow in simultaneous interpretation, especially alignment with shared content and sensitivity to first‑sentence delay, are key customer pain points.
contexts.resolution_hint: Use TTS acceleration, audio prefix, segmentation improvements, and TBT mode to mitigate perceived latency.

contexts.abstract: Tone and gender/voice mismatches in JP/KR raise RAI concerns.
contexts.text: Tone and naturalness issues in Japanese and Korean, along with occasional gender/voice mismatches where voice simulation is off, create user dissatisfaction and Responsible AI risks.
contexts.resolution_hint: Improve tone control and voice selection for JP/KR and add guardrails against misgendering and harassment.

contexts.abstract: SIM semantic mode and TTS acceleration improve quality and latency.
contexts.text: Simultaneous Interpreter (SIM) has semantic mode enabled in lower rings and TTS acceleration (1.2×–1.35×) to reduce accumulated translated audio latency, with reliability around 99%+.

contexts.abstract: TBT R0 is available with strong JP/KR feedback but 25‑session limit.
contexts.text: Turn‑by‑Turn Interpreter Ring 0 is available; early Japanese and Korean customer and GBB feedback shows strong accuracy and clearer turn‑taking, with known limits including 25 concurrent sessions and edge‑case behaviors under complex turns.

contexts.abstract: SIM latency mitigations include speedup mode and audio prefix.
contexts.text: Latency and UX enhancements for SIM include speedup mode, an audio prefix before the first translation to mask round‑trip time, and auto‑update spoken language detection via multilingual STT.

contexts.abstract: Transcription++ elevates transcription into an enterprise understanding layer.
contexts.text: Transcription++ aims to elevate transcription into an enterprise understanding layer with a tiered model stack, stronger grounding and enrichment (global and custom dictionaries, dynamic vocabulary), governance‑by‑design, and multilingual by default.

contexts.abstract: Real‑time quality layer focuses on entity enrichment and latency mitigation.
contexts.text: A real‑time quality enhancement layer is being built around entity enrichment, latency mitigation (audio prefix, segmentation improvements), and a biasing/adaptation framework using global and custom dictionaries across languages.

contexts.abstract: Admin Center reporting and metering enable governance and value articulation.
contexts.text: Admin Center usage reporting (CFR) and metering integration are underway to provide visibility into tenant adoption, meeting types, and language pairs, laying the foundation for enterprise governance and value articulation.

contexts.abstract: Unified evaluation uses LLM‑as‑judge for end‑to‑end quality metrics.
contexts.text: Unified evaluation now uses LLM‑as‑judge metrics for transcription and interpreter, producing consistent semantic, tone, latency, and entity scores across models and enabling apples‑to‑apples comparisons and faster iteration.

contexts.abstract: Multi‑recognizer platform enables hot‑switching between model families.
contexts.text: A multi‑recognizer platform coming January 2026 for Teams will allow hot‑switching between STS and LRM/LLM‑based models, simplifying pipelines and enabling faster experimentation with Phi‑4, multimodal LLMs, and unified multilingual models.

contexts.abstract: GPU capacity and LLM onboarding timelines are key risks.
contexts.text: GPU capacity and substrate LLM onboarding timelines for real‑time models pose risks, requiring maintained fallback paths with compliance controls.
contexts.resolution_hint: Secure GPU allocations, stage LLM onboarding, and harden fallback paths with compliance guardrails.

contexts.abstract: Admin reporting data ownership and latency need alignment.
contexts.text: Admin reporting CFR data cooking ownership and data latency require alignment between IDEAs and PM on contracts, creating a governance and accountability gap.
contexts.resolution_hint: Clarify ownership, SLAs, and contracts for CFR data pipelines between engineering and PM.

contexts.abstract: Responsible AI risks include harassment and misgendering.
contexts.text: Responsible AI risks include harassment and misgendering due to tone and gender defaults in speech translation models, particularly in JP/KR, requiring guardrails and tone control improvements.
contexts.resolution_hint: Implement RAI guardrails, monitoring, and tone control features for sensitive locales.

contexts.abstract: North star is >80% CSAT for interpreter with SIM and TBT modes.
contexts.text: The north star is to achieve over 80% CSAT for interpreter experiences by using SIM for fluid conversations, TBT for structured discussions, and eventually automatic mode switching based on meeting context.

contexts.abstract: Interpreter MAU is 136k with +1.9% MoM growth.
contexts.label: Interpreter MAU
contexts.context: Latest Interpreter KPI snapshot shows 136k monthly active users, +1.9% month‑over‑month.

contexts.label: Interpreter WAU
contexts.context: Latest Interpreter KPI snapshot shows 38.3k weekly active users, −2.5% week‑over‑week.

contexts.abstract: Monthly meeting count is 106k with +5.4% MoM growth.
contexts.label: Monthly Interpreter Meeting Count
contexts.context: Latest Interpreter KPI snapshot shows 106k monthly meetings, +5.4% month‑over‑month.

contexts.abstract: >5‑min meeting rate is 62.2% with +2.1% MoM.
contexts.label: >5‑min Meeting Rate
contexts.context: Latest Interpreter KPI snapshot shows 62.2% of meetings longer than 5 minutes, +2.1% month‑over‑month.

contexts.abstract: E2E reliability is 99.38% with +0.2% MoM.
contexts.label: E2E Interpreter Reliability
contexts.context: Latest Interpreter KPI snapshot shows 99.38% end‑to‑end reliability, +0.2% month‑over‑month.

contexts.abstract: Interpreter CSAT is 71% with −2% MoM.
contexts.label: Interpreter CSAT
contexts.context: Latest Interpreter KPI snapshot shows 71% customer satisfaction, −2% month‑over‑month.

contexts.abstract: Multilingual STT entity recall improved from 65.42 to 74.76.
contexts.label: Entity Recall (Type II, PPE tests)
contexts.context: Observed improvements in batch S2S entity accuracy for multilingual STT.

contexts.abstract: Post‑meeting inaccuracy reduced from 19.5% to 12.3% (−37%).
contexts.label: Overall Transcription Inaccuracy
contexts.context: Impact of post‑meeting Transcript Enricher R4 rollout.

contexts.abstract: Domain entity errors decreased by 34% with Enricher.
contexts.label: Domain Entity Error Reduction
contexts.context: Measured benefit from post‑meeting Transcript Enricher.

contexts.abstract: Accent/dialect issues decreased by 31% with Enricher.
contexts.label: Accent/Dialect Error Reduction
contexts.context: Measured benefit from post‑meeting Transcript Enricher.

contexts.abstract: CSAT increased from 42.95% to 62.32% after Enricher.
contexts.label: Transcription CSAT
contexts.context: Customer satisfaction improvement attributed to Transcript Enricher.

contexts.abstract: Target interpreter CSAT is >80% vs current 71%.
contexts.label: Target Interpreter CSAT
contexts.context: North star goal compared to current 71% CSAT.

contexts.abstract: Vision tagline: unified real‑time multilingual understanding in Teams.
contexts.quote: Next‑Gen Speech Intelligence in Teams — a unified vision for real‑time multilingual understanding across meetings, calls, and future AI agents.
contexts.context: Framing statement for 6–12 month vision & strategy section.

contexts.abstract: TBT uses GPT‑4o‑realtime and Azure Voice Live API for better tone.
contexts.text: The model stack for TBT uses GPT‑4o‑realtime plus Azure Voice Live API, producing notably improved semantic and tone accuracy per vNext evaluation.

contexts.abstract: Tier‑1 custom dictionary is GA; global dictionary under integration.
contexts.text: Tier‑1 custom dictionary is fully GA, while a global dictionary is under integration with dataset availability pending cluster issues; early multilingual entity adaptation recall is around 50% for JP/EN.

contexts.abstract: Vision includes unified multilingual model for transcription and interpretation.
contexts.text: The strategy includes deploying a unified multilingual model for both transcription and interpretation, exploring Phi‑4 multimodal and GPT‑4o for high‑value scenarios to simplify architecture and improve consistency.

contexts.description: A KPI dashboard slide showing MAU, WAU, monthly meeting count, >5‑min meeting rate, E2E reliability, and CSAT with MoM/WoW deltas for Interpreter.

content.headline: Interpreter usage is growing with strong reliability but modest satisfaction
content.subtitle: Interpreter is now a meaningful, stable surface shaping Copilot and Recap value
content.speaker_intent: Reinforce that this is a real, scaled surface with upside, not an experiment.

bullets.text: 136k MAU (+1.9% MoM) and 106k monthly meetings (+5.4% MoM) show sustained adoption.
>5‑minute meetings at 62.2% (+2.1% MoM) indicate deep usage in longer, higher‑value sessions.
E2E reliability at 99.38% (+0.2% MoM) meets enterprise expectations for stability.
CSAT at 71% (−2% MoM) signals value but also persistent friction in critical experiences.
Transcript quality directly affects Copilot and Recap DSAT; better speech lifts downstream AI satisfaction.
Admin reporting and metering workstreams are in progress but not yet fully exposing value to customers.

slides.story: Complication: make the pain vivid and economically meaningful

content.headline: Accuracy, latency, and tone gaps are eroding trust in high‑stakes meetings
content.subtitle: Current SIM and transcription limitations create a crisis of inaction for multilingual enterprises
content.speaker_intent: Shift the room from comfort with current reliability to urgency about experience gaps.

bullets.text: Technical terms, names, and numbers/units are frequently wrong; translations feel too literal in SIM, especially for JP/KR.
Latency issues—slow first sentence and misaligned segments with shared content—break meeting flow.
Tone and gender mismatches in JP/KR, including rare harassment/misgendering risks, damage trust and brand.
Interpreted audio is not captured in recordings; cross‑tenant/guest licensing remains confusing for customers.
High‑stakes meetings (board, public sector, enterprise reviews) cannot rely on SIM alone, driving human‑interp fallback pressure.
Imperfect transcripts degrade Copilot/Recap grounding, inflating DSAT and limiting AI upsell potential.
Limited governance (usage visibility, quality reporting) makes it harder for enterprises to standardize on Teams for multilingual work.

slides.story: Question: crystallize the strategic problem and preview the answer
slides.visual_design: LayoutStacked: top=short narrative, bottom=3-bullet framing of strategic question and answer

content.headline: We must turn fragmented speech features into a unified multilingual intelligence layer
content.subtitle: The question is how to close critical gaps while scaling quality and governance
content.speaker_intent: Set up the unified stack as the inevitable answer, not one more feature set.

bullets.text: How do we deliver interpreter experiences that customers trust for board‑level and public sector meetings, not just casual calls?
How do we systematically improve entity accuracy and tone so Copilot and Recap become reliably valuable, not hit‑or‑miss?
How do we give enterprises governance, reporting, and recording parity so they can standardize on Teams for multilingual work?
Unify Interpreter, Captions, and Transcription on a multilingual‑by‑default stack with entity accuracy as the north star.
Layer SIM and Turn‑by‑Turn Interpreter (TBT) for different meeting types, powered by next‑gen models and enrichment.
Embed governance, reporting, and recording parity to articulate value and meet enterprise compliance needs.

slides.story: Answer: present the unified architecture and 6–12 month vision
slides.visual_design: LayoutSplit5050: left=layered architecture diagram (speech capture → multilingual STT → Interpreter/TBT → Enricher → Copilot/Recap/Admin), right=SmartList summarizing 6–12 month strategy

content.headline: A unified speech stack will power reliable multilingual meetings and AI
content.subtitle: One multilingual backbone for Captions, Transcription, and Interpreter, tuned for entities and governance
content.speaker_intent: Show that the solution is coherent, already in motion, and focused on measurable outcomes.

bullets.text: Single multilingual STT endpoint with auto language detection and code‑switch tolerance as the foundation.
Interpreter layer with dual modes: SIM for fluid conversations; TBT for structured, high‑stakes discussions.
Transcript Enricher as a real‑time and post‑meeting quality layer correcting names and domain entities.
Shared entity infrastructure (global + custom dictionaries, dynamic vocabulary) feeding both STT and Interpreter.
Governance layer with metering, admin reporting, quality gates, and recording parity for interpreted audio.
Make entity accuracy the north star, with Enricher in‑meeting and post‑meeting across top locales.
Broaden language and tone coverage (e.g., zh‑TW, JP/KR quality) to win head‑to‑head in key markets.
Strengthen governance with Admin Center dashboards, metering, and ringed rollout discipline.
Explore offline/fast catch‑up transcription to reduce CoGS while preserving enterprise‑grade experience.
Deliver recording parity for interpreted audio (multi‑track options) to unlock multilingual recap and compliance scenarios.

slides.story: Answer: deep dive on Interpreter SIM + TBT as the core user experience
slides.visual_design: LayoutDashboard: main=2-column comparison (SIM vs TBT), sidebar=small table of latest metrics and capabilities

content.headline: Interpreter SIM and TBT together resolve flow, accuracy, and control gaps
content.subtitle: SIM for continuous flow; TBT for turn precision in formal and public sector meetings
content.speaker_intent: Demonstrate that we have a concrete, feasible plan to fix the biggest meeting‑flow pain points.

bullets.text: Semantic mode enabled in lower rings improves long‑segment coherence and semantic‑level translation.
TTS acceleration (1.2×–1.35×) and audio prefix reduce perceived latency and accumulated translated audio lag.
Auto‑update spoken language detection via multilingual STT reduces mis‑detects and manual switching friction.
Calling and MTR support is live across rings; CSS meeting‑level license checks enabled for the first support group.
TBT R0 is available; early JP/KR customer and GBB feedback shows stronger accuracy and clearer turn‑taking.
Model stack uses GPT‑4o‑realtime with Azure Voice Live API to improve semantic and tone accuracy.
TBT fixes core SIM pain points: reduces translation overlap, clarifies speakers, and supports structured discussions.
Known limits (25 concurrent sessions, complex turn edge cases) are identified for capacity and UX investments.
Expand TBT capacity, stabilize edge cases, and add UX cues for turn etiquette.
Establish evaluation pipelines for accuracy, tone, and flow across SIM and TBT using LLM‑based metrics.

slides.story: Answer: deep dive on transcription, multilingual STT, and enrichment as the accuracy engine
slides.visual_design: LayoutSplit5050: left=process flow diagram (raw audio → multilingual STT → Enricher → Copilot/Recap/Admin), right=SmartList with metrics and roadmap

content.headline: Multilingual STT and Enricher materially improve transcription and AI grounding
content.subtitle: Entity‑aware transcription is the backbone for Copilot, Recap, and Interpreter quality
content.speaker_intent: Show quantified gains and a credible path to further accuracy improvements.

bullets.text: Unified multi‑recognizer endpoint with auto language detection shipped to Ring 0 and Ring 1.
Supports 9 languages in preview with ongoing adaptation, phrase‑hint, and segmentation tuning.
Phrase hint fix mitigates freezes >800 ms; batch S2S entity recall improved from 65.42 to 74.76 in PPE tests.
Multilingual STT eliminates setup friction and unlocks bilingual meetings for global customers.
R4 rollout at 50% for EN/JP and 10% for FR/DE/PT/ES; 1.8M+ meetings weekly are enhanced.
Post‑meeting Enricher reduced overall transcription inaccuracy from 19.5% to 12.3% (37% reduction).
Domain entity errors dropped 34% and accent/dialect issues dropped 31%, driving CSAT from 42.95% to 62.32%.
In‑meeting enrichment architecture is aligned with R0 targeted for January 2026 and multilingual support planned for CY2026 Q1.
Tier‑1 custom dictionary is GA; global dictionary integration is in progress, with early JP/EN recall around 50% and improving.
Transcription++ elevates transcription into an enterprise understanding layer with tiered models and governance‑by‑design.
Tenant auto‑dictionary (SLPv2) and dynamic vocabulary will be integrated to further boost entity accuracy.

slides.story: Answer: deep dive on evaluation, models, and infrastructure proving feasibility and moat
slides.visual_design: LayoutDashboard: main=Sankey-style or flow chart of evaluation and multi-recognizer platform; sidebar=SmartList on business value and model roadmap

content.headline: Unified evaluation and multi‑recognizer infra make rapid quality gains feasible
content.subtitle: LLM‑based metrics and flexible infrastructure de‑risk next‑gen model adoption
content.speaker_intent: Reassure LT that the plan is buildable and we can choose the best models pragmatically.

bullets.text: LLM‑as‑judge metrics now assess transcription and interpreter on semantic quality, tone, latency, and entities.
Supports apples‑to‑apples comparison across ST, Semantic, Phi, GPT‑4o real‑time, TBT pipeline, and multilingual STT.
Accelerates iteration cycles, reduces human eval cost, and improves rollout decisions with transparent tradeoffs for LT.
Phi‑4‑based streaming translation for SIM shows early promise in long‑segment semantic reasoning.
Teams and Speech are exploring unified multilingual models and GPT‑4o for high‑value scenarios.
Phi‑4 and LLM multimodal approaches are positioned to complement ST‑based streaming models, not replace them outright.
Multi‑recognizer platform for Teams coming January 2026 enables hot‑switching between STS and LRM/LLM‑based models.
Simplifies pipelines, supports unified multilingual models, and unlocks faster experimentation across rings.
Resource expansion from 10 to 20 environments is being evaluated to support global reliability and experimentation.

content.headline: Governance, reporting, and recording parity will unlock enterprise standardization
content.subtitle: Making usage, quality, and interpreted audio visible and compliant for admins
content.speaker_intent: Connect technical roadmap to the governance and compliance levers executives care about.

bullets.text: Admin Center usage reporting (CFR) and metering integration are underway to surface tenant adoption and meeting types.
Usage dashboards public preview is targeted for March 31, 2026, with metering validation in progress.
These capabilities will enable enterprise governance and value articulation across language pairs and workloads.
Recording parity for interpreted audio (multi‑track options) is part of the 6–12 month vision.
This unlocks multilingual recap and compliance scenarios that are currently blocked by missing interpreted tracks.
Cross‑tenant/guest licensing clarity is a known gap and will be addressed alongside governance improvements.
Guardrails for harassment and misgendering risks are being tracked as explicit Responsible AI workstreams.
Tone control improvements in JP/KR are a focus area to meet market‑specific expectations and avoid brand risk.

slides.story: Risks & Asks: surface key dependencies and decisions needed from LT
slides.visual_design: LayoutStacked: top=Risk table using Harvey Balls for severity/mitigation, bottom=explicit LT asks list

content.headline: Targeted LT support will de‑risk GPU, data, and RAi dependencies
content.subtitle: Clear asks around capacity, data ownership, and guardrails to deliver the unified stack
content.speaker_intent: Convert concerns into concrete support decisions and show that risks are understood and managed.

bullets.text: GPU capacity and substrate LLM onboarding timelines may constrain real‑time models for SIM/TBT; fallback paths must remain compliant.
Single points of failure and error‑handling maturity across rings and environments require tighter incident monitoring alignment.
Admin reporting CFR data cooking ownership and data latency are unclear, risking delays to governance features.
Responsible AI gaps in tone control (JP/KR) and rare harassment/misgendering cases must be proactively mitigated.
Prioritize GPU allocation and substrate LLM onboarding for real‑time Interpreter and STT workloads.
Align incident monitoring and SPOF remediation across Teams, Speech, and Voice Live API environments.
Clarify CFR data ownership between IDEAs and PM, including contracts for latency and freshness SLAs.
Endorse Responsible AI investments for JP/KR tone control and harassment guardrails as non‑negotiable quality bars.

sections.title: What We Will Deliver in 6–12 Months

bullets.text: Unified speech stack across Captions, Transcription, and Interpreter with multilingual STT as the backbone.
SIM + TBT Interpreter with improved latency, tone, and entity accuracy for both fluid and structured meetings.
Entity‑aware Transcription++ and Enricher, plus governance, reporting, and recording parity for enterprise adoption.
Finalize TBT capacity plan and SIM semantic rollout using LLM‑based evaluation to guide model choices.
Complete Enricher GA for Tier‑1 locales and integrate tenant auto‑dictionary and dynamic vocabulary.
Lock GPU and LLM onboarding commitments, CFR data ownership, and RAi workstreams with LT sponsorship.
